By the end of this lesson, you can:

Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

always — every time. Example: I always drink water.
usually — most of the time. Example: She usually walks to work.
often — many times. Example: We often eat fish.
sometimes — on some occasions. Example: I sometimes watch films.
never — not at any time. Example: He never drinks coffee.
habit — something you do regularly. Example: Reading is a good habit.
morning — the early part of the day. Example: Good morning, class!
evening — the later part of the day. Example: Good evening, Mrs Brown.
weekend — Saturday and Sunday. Example: I relax at the weekend.
every day — each day. Example: I study English every day.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I always wake up early. (talking about a habit)
• She usually drinks coffee. (talking about another person's habit)
• We sometimes go to the cinema. (talking about frequency)
• He never goes to bed late. (talking about a negative habit)
• How often do you...? (asking about frequency)
• Do you ever...? (asking about frequency)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'every time'?
Which word means 'most of the time'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use adverbs of frequency to say how often something happens.

Form:
Adverbs of frequency: always (100%), usually (80%), often (60%), sometimes (30%), never (0%). Put them before the main verb, but after 'be'.

Examples:
• I always wake up early.
• She usually drinks tea.
• We sometimes go to the cinema.
• He is never late.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I ___ drink coffee. (100%)
She ___ goes to bed late. (0%)
He is ___ tired. (often)
We ___ eat fish. (30%)
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I ... (always / usually / sometimes / never) ...
• My ... (always / usually / sometimes / never) ...
• I am ... (always / usually / never) ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you always do in the morning?
• What do you never do on Sunday?
• How often do you go to the cinema?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your habits with frequency adverbs.
• Write three sentences about a friend's habits with frequency adverbs.
Reading: Who does it?

I always wake up early. My brother usually drinks coffee. My sister often goes to the gym. We sometimes go to the cinema on Saturday. My father never goes to bed late on weekdays. What about you? How often do you exercise? Do you ever study at the weekend?
What does the brother usually drink?
When does the family sometimes go to the cinema?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How often do you exercise?
B: I usually exercise three times a week.
A: Do you ever go to the gym?
B: Sometimes, but I never go on Sunday.
A: And how often do you study English?
B: I study English every day!
How often does the speaker exercise?
When does the speaker never go to the gym?
Speaking task: Ask your partner five 'How often...?' questions and note the answers. Report two answers to the class.

• How often do you exercise?
• How often do you drink coffee?
• Do you ever study at the weekend?
• What do you always do in the morning?
• What do you never do?
Role-play: You are a health coach. Ask a client about their habits and give two simple suggestions.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your habits with frequency adverbs.
Model: I always ... I usually ... I sometimes ... I never ...
